claims.text: The initial high-entropy alloy is a single-phase solid solution.
The intervention introduces a coherent L12 phase into the high-entropy alloy.
A coherent L12 phase can act as an effective strengthener in high-entropy alloys.
Introducing coherent L12 improves resistance to thermally induced toughness loss.
The coherent L12 phase reduces void formation.
The coherent L12 phase increases the alloy's overall strength.
Reducing void formation increases resistance to thermally induced toughness loss.
Increasing overall strength increases resistance to thermally induced toughness loss.
Relative to an otherwise comparable alloy without coherent L12, the modified alloy will have greater strength at elevated temperatures.
Relative to an otherwise comparable alloy without coherent L12, the modified alloy will have greater toughness at elevated temperatures.
Relative to the baseline, the modified alloy will experience less thermally induced toughness loss.
The strengthening phase must remain sufficiently stable for the hypothesized benefit to hold.
The alloy must avoid decomposition into multiple phases for the hypothesized benefit to hold.
The exact mechanism linking coherent L12 to resistance against thermally induced toughness loss is not fully understood.

contradictions.description: The intervention intentionally introduces an L12 phase into an initially single-phase solid solution, creating at least a matrix-plus-L12 microstructure, while the boundary says decomposition into multiple phases must be avoided. The wording does not distinguish desired L12 precipitation from undesired decomposition.
